description: Found investigating fz-sc8.225. IO.inspect(%{__struct__: S, a: 1, b: [2]}) prints %{__struct__: S, a: 1, b: [2]} on every path; Elixir prints %S{a: 1, b: [2]}. The runtime already prints a map whose keys are exactly S's fields as %S{} when S's schema is registered (MapView::named_schema); the program lacks the schema. Each executable lists the modules its types name under __struct__ (Types::struct_modules), and jobs/backend.rs includes a schema only when StructDefined(S) happens to be settled already, a read with no wait. Fix (proposal https://claude.ai/artifact/XpsXXTqWBG6Skjq5Hi2JH6, approach A): for each such module that can be defined (has source, or is a runtime module), the backend waits on ModuleDefined(S); StructDefined is DefineModule's co-output, so after it the answer is final and the schema is included when S declares a struct. Not StructDefined directly: for a module with no struct that wait ends in 'module is not a struct'. A name no source defines is not a struct and nothing waits. Probed with .239: full suite green, distiller pins unchanged. Done when: an oracle fixture with no %S{} anywhere prints %S{...} for a literal, a Map.put of __struct__, and an unquoted Macro.escape of a struct, and a map for a missing field, a module with no struct and an unknown name, on interp, run and build.
title: A map literal that spells a struct builds that struct
